NASB.1: Then Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
NASB.2: Now when Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard [of it], he was living in Egypt (for he was yet in Egypt, where he had fled from the presence of King Solomon).
NASB.3: Then they sent and called him, and Jeroboam and all the assembly of Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
NASB.4: 'Your father made our yoke hard; now therefore lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke which he put on us, and we will serve you.'
NASB.5: Then he said to them, 'Depart for three days, then return to me.' So the people departed.
NASB.6: King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had served his father Solomon while he was still alive, saying, 'How do you counsel [me] to answer this people?'
NASB.7: Then they spoke to him, saying, 'If you will be a servant to this people today, and will serve them and grant them their petition, and speak good words to them, then they will be your servants forever.'
NASB.8: But he forsook the counsel of the elders which they had given him, and consulted with the young men who grew up with him and served him.
NASB.9: So he said to them, 'What counsel do you give that we may answer this people who have spoken to me, saying, 'Lighten the yoke which your father put on us'?'
NASB.10: The young men who grew up with him spoke to him, saying, 'Thus you shall say to this people who spoke to you, saying, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, now you make it lighter for us!' But you shall speak to them, 'My little finger is thicker than my father's loins!
NASB.11: 'Whereas my father loaded you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke; my father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.''
NASB.12: Then Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day as the king had directed, saying, 'Return to me on the third day.'
NASB.13: The king answered the people harshly, for he forsook the advice of the elders which they had given him,
NASB.14: and he spoke to them according to the advice of the young men, saying, 'My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to your yoke; my father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.'
NASB.15: So the king did not listen to the people; for it was a turn [of events] from the LORD, that He might establish His word, which the LORD spoke through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
NASB.16: When all Israel [saw] that the king did not listen to them, the people answered the king, saying, 'What portion do we have in David? [We have] no inheritance in the son of Jesse; To your tents, O Israel! Now look after your own house, David!' So Israel departed to their tents.
NASB.17: But as for the sons of Israel who lived in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.
NASB.18: Then King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the forced labor, and all Israel stoned him to death. And King Rehoboam made haste to mount his chariot to flee to Jerusalem.
NASB.19: So Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.
NASB.20: It came about when all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, that they sent and called him to the assembly and made him king over all Israel. None but the tribe of Judah followed the house of David.
NASB.21: Now when Rehoboam had come to Jerusalem, he assembled all the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, 180,000 chosen men who were warriors, to fight against the house of Israel to restore the kingdom to Rehoboam the son of Solomon.
NASB.22: But the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying,
NASB.23: 'Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin and to the rest of the people, saying,
NASB.24: 'Thus says the LORD, 'You must not go up and fight against your relatives the sons of Israel; return every man to his house, for this thing has come from Me.''' So they listened to the word of the LORD, and returned and went [their way] according to the word of the LORD.
NASB.25: Then Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and lived there. And he went out from there and built Penuel.
NASB.26: Jeroboam said in his heart, 'Now the kingdom will return to the house of David.
NASB.27: 'If this people go up to offer sacrifices in the house of the LORD at Jerusalem, then the heart of this people will return to their lord, [even] to Rehoboam king of Judah; and they will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah.'
NASB.28: So the king consulted, and made two golden calves, and he said to them, 'It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem; behold your gods, O Israel, that brought you up from the land of Egypt.'
NASB.29: He set one in Bethel, and the other he put in Dan.
NASB.30: Now this thing became a sin, for the people went [to worship] before the one as far as Dan.
NASB.31: And he made houses on high places, and made priests from among all the people who were not of the sons of Levi.
NASB.32: Jeroboam instituted a feast in the eighth month on the fifteenth day of the month, like the feast which is in Judah, and he went up to the altar; thus he did in Bethel, sacrificing to the calves which he had made. And he stationed in Bethel the priests of the high places which he had made.
NASB.33: Then he went up to the altar which he had made in Bethel on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, even in the month which he had devised in his own heart; and he instituted a feast for the sons of Israel and went up to the altar to burn incense.

NLT.1: Rehoboam went to Shechem, where all Israel had gathered to make him king.
NLT.2: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard of this, he returned from Egypt, for he had fled to Egypt to escape from King Solomon.
NLT.3: The leaders of Israel summoned him, and Jeroboam and the whole assembly of Israel went to speak with Rehoboam.
NLT.4: “Your father was a hard master,” they said. “Lighten the harsh labor demands and heavy taxes that your father imposed on us. Then we will be your loyal subjects.”
NLT.5: Rehoboam replied, “Give me three days to think this over. Then come back for my answer.” So the people went away.
NLT.6: Then King Rehoboam discussed the matter with the older men who had counseled his father, Solomon. “What is your advice?” he asked. “How should I answer these people?”
NLT.7: The older counselors replied, “If you are willing to be a servant to these people today and give them a favorable answer, they will always be your loyal subjects.”
NLT.8: But Rehoboam rejected the advice of the older men and instead asked the opinion of the young men who had grown up with him and were now his advisers.
NLT.9: “What is your advice?” he asked them. “How should I answer these people who want me to lighten the burdens imposed by my father?”
NLT.10: The young men replied, “This is what you should tell those complainers who want a lighter burden: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!
NLT.11: Yes, my father laid heavy burdens on you, but I’m going to make them even heavier! My father beat you with whips, but I will beat you with scorpions!’”
NLT.12: Three days later Jeroboam and all the people returned to hear Rehoboam’s decision, just as the king had ordered.
NLT.13: But Rehoboam spoke harshly to the people, for he rejected the advice of the older counselors
NLT.14: and followed the counsel of his younger advisers. He told the people, “My father laid heavy burdens on you, but I’m going to make them even heavier! My father beat you with whips, but I will beat you with scorpions!”
NLT.15: So the king paid no attention to the people. This turn of events was the will of the LORD, for it fulfilled the LORD’s message to Jeroboam son of Nebat through the prophet Ahijah from Shiloh.
NLT.16:
When all Israel realized that the king had refused to listen to them, they responded, “Down with the dynasty of David!
We have no interest in the son of Jesse.
Back to your homes, O Israel!
Look out for your own house, O David!”
So the people of Israel returned home.
NLT.17: But Rehoboam continued to rule over the Israelites who lived in the towns of Judah.
NLT.18: King Rehoboam sent Adoniram, who was in charge of forced labor, to restore order, but the people of Israel stoned him to death. When this news reached King Rehoboam, he quickly jumped into his chariot and fled to Jerusalem.
NLT.19: And to this day the northern tribes of Israel have refused to be ruled by a descendant of David.
NLT.20: When the people of Israel learned of Jeroboam’s return from Egypt, they called an assembly and made him king over all Israel. So only the tribe of Judah remained loyal to the family of David.
NLT.21: When Rehoboam arrived at Jerusalem, he mobilized the men of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin — 180,000 select troops — to fight against the men of Israel and to restore the kingdom to himself.
NLT.22: But God said to Shemaiah, the man of God,
NLT.23: “Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the people of Judah and Benjamin, and to the rest of the people,
NLT.24: ‘This is what the LORD says: Do not fight against your relatives, the Israelites. Go back home, for what has happened is my doing!’” So they obeyed the message of the LORD and went home, as the LORD had commanded.
NLT.25: Jeroboam then built up the city of Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and it became his capital. Later he went and built up the town of Peniel.
NLT.26: Jeroboam thought to himself, “Unless I am careful, the kingdom will return to the dynasty of David.
NLT.27: When these people go to Jerusalem to offer sacrifices at the Temple of the LORD, they will again give their allegiance to King Rehoboam of Judah. They will kill me and make him their king instead.”
NLT.28: So on the advice of his counselors, the king made two gold calves. He said to the people, “It is too much trouble for you to worship in Jerusalem. Look, Israel, these are the gods who brought you out of Egypt!”
NLT.29: He placed these calf idols in Bethel and in Dan — at either end of his kingdom.
NLT.30: But this became a great sin, for the people worshiped the idols, traveling as far north as Dan to worship the one there.
NLT.31: Jeroboam also erected buildings at the pagan shrines and ordained priests from the common people — those who were not from the priestly tribe of Levi.
NLT.32: And Jeroboam instituted a religious festival in Bethel, held on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, in imitation of the annual Festival of Shelters in Judah. There at Bethel he himself offered sacrifices to the calves he had made, and he appointed priests for the pagan shrines he had made.
NLT.33: So on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, a day that he himself had designated, Jeroboam offered sacrifices on the altar at Bethel. He instituted a religious festival for Israel, and he went up to the altar to burn incense.

AMP.1: Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
AMP.2: Now when Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard about it, he was living in Egypt (for he was still in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon).
AMP.3: So they sent word and called for him, and Jeroboam and all the assembly of Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,
AMP.4: "Your father made our yoke (burden) heavy; so now lighten the hard labor and the heavy yoke your father imposed on us, and we will serve you."
AMP.5: Rehoboam replied to them, "Leave for three days, then come back to me [for my decision]." So the people left.
AMP.6: King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had served and advised his father Solomon while he was still alive and said, "How do you advise me to answer this people?"
AMP.7: They spoke to him, saying, "If you will be a servant to this people today, and will serve them and grant their request, and speak good words to them, then they will be your servants forever."
AMP.8: But he ignored the advice which the elders gave him and consulted the young men who grew up with him and served him.
AMP.9: He said to them, "What do you advise that we answer this people who have said to me, 'Lighten the yoke (burden) which your father put on us'?"
AMP.10: The young men who had grown up with him answered, "This is what you should say to this people who told you, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, but as for you, make our yoke lighter'—say this to them: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's loins [and my reign will be even more severe].
AMP.11: And now, whereas my father loaded you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.'"
AMP.12: Jeroboam and all the people came back to Rehoboam on the third day, just as the king had instructed, saying, "Return to me on the third day."
AMP.13: The king answered the people harshly and ignored the advice which the elders had given him,
AMP.14: and spoke to them in accordance with the advice of the young men, saying, "My father made your yoke heavy, but as for me, I will add to your yoke; my father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions."
AMP.15: So the king did not listen to the people; for the situation was from the LORD, so that He might fulfill His word which He spoke through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
AMP.16:
So when all [the ten northern tribes of] Israel saw that the king did not listen to them, the people replied to the king, saying,
"What portion do we have in David?
We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse;
To your tents, O Israel!
Look now after your own house, David!"
Then Israel went back to their tents.
AMP.17: But as for the sons (descendants) of Israel who lived in the cities of Judah [including Benjamin], Rehoboam reigned over them.
AMP.18: Then King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was in charge of the forced labor [to represent him], and all Israel stoned him to death. And King Rehoboam quickly mounted his chariot to escape to Jerusalem.
AMP.19: So Israel (the ten northern tribes) has rebelled against the house (royal line) of David to this day (the date of this writing).
AMP.20: It came about when all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, that they sent word and called him to the assembly and made him king over all Israel. None followed the house of David except the tribe of Judah [including Benjamin].
AMP.21: Now when Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he assembled all the [fighting men from the] house of Judah, with the tribe of Benjamin, 180,000 chosen warriors, to fight against the house of Israel to bring the kingdom back to Rehoboam the son of Solomon.
AMP.22: But the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying,
AMP.23: "Tell Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and all the house (fighting men) of Judah and Benjamin and the rest of the people,
AMP.24: 'Thus says the LORD, "You shall not go up and fight against your brothers, the sons of Israel. Let every man return to his house, for this thing has come about from Me."'" So they listened to the word of the LORD and returned to go home, in accordance with the word of the LORD.
AMP.25: Then Jeroboam built Shechem [as his royal city] in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. He went out from there and rebuilt Penuel [as a stronghold].
AMP.26: Jeroboam [doubted God's promise to him and] said in his heart, "Now the kingdom will return to the house of David.
AMP.27: If these people go up to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem to offer sacrifices, then their heart will turn to their lord, to Rehoboam king of Judah; and they will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah."
AMP.28: So the king took counsel [and followed bad advice] and made two calves of gold. And he said to the people, "It is too much for you to go [all the way] up to Jerusalem; behold your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt."
AMP.29: He set the one [golden calf] in Bethel, and the other he put in Dan.
AMP.30: Now this thing became a sin [for Israel]; because the people went to worship before the one [or the other of them] as far as Dan.
AMP.31: And Jeroboam also made houses on high places, and he made priests from all people who were not of the sons (descendants) of Levi.
AMP.32: Jeroboam held a feast on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, like the feast which is kept in Judah, and he went up to the altar; he did this in Bethel, sacrificing to the calves which he had made. And he stationed in Bethel the priests of the high places which he had made.
AMP.33: So he went up to the altar which he had made in Bethel on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, in the month which he had devised in his own heart [in defiance of God's commandments]; and he held a feast for the Israelites and he went up to the altar to burn incense [in defiance of God's law.]

WEB.1: Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.

WEB.4: “Your father made our yoke difficult. Now therefore make the hard service of your father, and his heavy yoke which he put on us, lighter, and we will serve you.”

WEB.12: So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam the third day, as the king asked, saying, “Come to me again the third day.”
WEB.13: The king answered the people roughly, and abandoned the counsel of the old men which they had given him,
